spec_family.name: New Construction Drywall Ceiling Prime Coat
spec_family.description: PVA or drywall primer on new drywall ceilings in new construction. Covers flat ceilings, tray ceiling flat areas, and vaulted/cathedral ceiling areas. Separate from wall prime (different overhead application considerations) and ceiling finish (prime happens before trim install). Single primer coat, no finish coats.

includes: New drywall ceiling field area (flat ceilings)
Tray ceiling flat areas (treated as standard ceiling field)
Vaulted/cathedral ceiling flat areas (height modifier applies)
excludes: Textured ceiling application (pre-paint trade, out of scope)
Stain blocking for smoke/water damage (use repaint spec)

configuration_dimensions.description: Drives inspection intensity and edge precision. Does NOT differentiate primer application — primer must be applied properly at all tiers.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT2: minimal prep, relaxed edge precision, sheen limited to eggshell. QT3: standard prep, clean edges. QT4: thorough prep, crisp edges. Application quality (drips/sags/holidays) is constant across all tiers.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for ceiling primer
configuration_dimensions.notes: Spray+backroll is standard for NC ceiling prime. Roll for smaller areas or occupied spaces. Spray-only less common on ceilings — backroll recommended for consolidation on overhead surfaces.

configuration_dimensions.description: Ceiling height classification driving access requirements and height modifiers
configuration_dimensions.notes: standard (≤9ft), tall (10-12ft), vaulted (13-17ft), cathedral (18ft+). Drives height modifier on production rates. More aggressive impact than wall height modifiers due to overhead work.

configuration_dimensions.description: Drywall finish level per GA-214 standard
configuration_dimensions.notes: Level 3 = tape/compound only; Level 4 = additional skim coat; Level 5 = skim coat entire surface

configuration_dimensions.description: Ceiling surface texture (if applied before priming)
configuration_dimensions.notes: Texture affects coverage rate and application technique. Smooth is most common for ceilings.

paintable_items.name: Ceiling Field Prime Coat
paintable_items.counting_rules: Source from PaintScope PS_SURFACE_SF.CEILING_FIELD; covers all paintable ceiling area
paintable_items.notes: Primary item for ceiling priming scope

paintable_items.name: Wall Edge Cut-In
paintable_items.counting_rules: Source from PaintScope PS_EDGE_LF.TO_CEILING; ceiling-to-wall boundary requiring brush cut-in. Same physical edge as wall spec's TO_CEILING key.
paintable_items.notes: Required when roll method used or spray requires edge touch-up at wall line

variants.notes: Minimal economy roller application — edge work not separated
Standard quality roller application with edge cut-in
Premium roller application with crisp edge work
Standard production spray+backroll with edge cut-in
Premium spray+backroll with attention to edge discipline
Economy spray-only, no backroll, edge work not separated
Standard spray-only where backroll not required

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Linear footage of ceiling-to-wall edge for cut-in work.
Floor area requiring protection during ceiling spray. Full room coverage.

protection_zones_required.notes: Ceiling overspray falls to floor across entire room. Full coverage mandatory for spray methods.
Roll method has minimal drip risk — perimeter drops sufficient.
Mask wall tops to prevent ceiling primer from running down wall face. In NC, walls are typically bare — protection prevents contamination of bare drywall.
Any fixtures installed before priming need protection from overspray.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Crown typically not installed during prime phase in NC. Included for completeness.

valid_input_states.notes: NC ceiling prime operates on bare new drywall only

output_state.notes: Ceiling prime produces field-primed state ready for finish coat

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: Full mask required for finished walls — solid tape line at wall-to-ceiling junction with draped plastic along wall. Rare in NC (ceilings primed before walls) but required for repaint scenarios.
Unfinished walls need no protection from ceiling primer

site_condition_rules.affects: Floor protection tasks — rosin paper on hard floors, plastic on carpet. Subfloor may not require protection.
Ceiling height determines access equipment and triggers height modifiers. Standard ceilings = none. Tall = step_ladder. Vaulted/cathedral = scaffold.

inherited_research_corrections.title: No spot-priming NC drywall fasteners
inherited_research_corrections.impact: No spot-prime tasks — same reasoning as wall prime

inherited_research_corrections.title: PVA/acrylic drywall primers have zero stain blocking
inherited_research_corrections.impact: No stain blocking claims in materials

inherited_research_corrections.title: Floor protection conditional on floor_type
inherited_research_corrections.impact: Site condition rules for floor_type apply. Ceiling spray always requires floor_full.

inherited_research_corrections.title: Do not specify dry times in specs

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec family for NC drywall ceiling priming. Generated from brief specs/_backlog/SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_NC_PRIME/brief.md. Mirrors SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_PRIME structure with ceiling-specific overhead rate reductions (15-25%), floor_full protection for spray, height modifiers per Modifier_Registry, and edge key resolution (uses PS_EDGE_LF.TO_CEILING for same physical edge).
